I just got a new 2016 Ford Fiesta about a week ago, and I was wondering if anybody had tips on maintaining a car so it'll last. I know the basics of checking fluids and rotating tires, but beyond that my mechanical/cosmetic skills are lacking.

What are your best tips for keeping a car in (near) new condition?

It is hard for me to care about a Ford Fiesta (sorry) but besides the basics with your fluids, there's not really a lot you need to know about nowadays unless you want to get into tuning and modifying. They're usually designed nowadays specifically for people who don't want to work on cars. Maybe obvious stuff about not driving it super hard like doing 90 over speedbumps.

But in terms of cosmetics I would say, don't allow any food or drinks to be consumed in your car. I'll make an exception on road trips sometimes but I'm pretty militant about that policy. Use a sunshade in your windshield. Don't keep anything in your car that isn't tucked away in some compartment. No books, no kid's toys, no random papers or cords or anything. It might not seem important but a lack of clutter can make older cars seem somehow newer than they really are. Also don't use automatic car washes. Hand wash or go to a place where they do that and where they will vacuum and wipe down the inside. Do it often.

No offence taken on the for fiesta part, I'm in college and do a lot of commuting for work so I needed a car with better gas mileage. Not my dream car but it works for me.

I figured fluids would be about it, but I'm coming from an old bronco which required around the clock care to keep running.

I'm usually pretty good about keeping the inside clean and I'm only taking water into my car, no food or drink otherwise. I'll look into a sun shade though. Thanks for the tip.

EDITS: phone kept hitting save
Also I guess there's other semi routine maintenance stuff like plugs/wires, brakes, but somehow that got lumped in with fluids in my head as basic stuff you already know about.

Wash off the road salt from the undercarriage in the winter. To better access the underbody, it helps if you buy ramps.

Also make sure you change your timing belt somewhere between 60K -120K miles.

If your car is turbocharged it might be a better idea to use synthetic oil.
